parsed.explanation: Count check: the first j+1 columns d,2d,...,2^j d contain 2^{j+1}-1 strips of height d; 'two identical copies of all preceding strips plus one' would be 2^{j+2}-1 strips, while the next column 2^{j+1}d has exactly 2^{j+1}. The stated structural reason for the inductive step is arithmetically false for every j (even j=0: 3 vs 2, so the objector's parenthetical actually understates). No other justification is offered, and the only prior fact about cuts is 'a cut can interchange the two parity rows only above its level'; nothing reconciles cuts at arbitrary non-multiple-of-d heights with the 'whole d-strip remains' dichotomy. Thus 'an odd strip therefore remains' does not follow. Lemma (ii) is not proved elsewhere in the text, and Section 3's lower bound rests entirely on it, so the lower-bound obligation fails as written.
